chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah from Musa ibn Imran from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed Al-Nawfaly from Al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

A man from the people of Al-Qadar (those who believe in Divine Decree/Capacity) asked him, saying: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah! Inform me about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And to Allah is due the Hajj of the House for whoever is able to find a way to it.' Is it not that Allah has made the capacity for them?' He said: 'Woe to you! What is meant by 'capacity' is the provisions and the mount; it is not the capacity of the body.'

The man said: 'Is it not so that when there are provisions and a mount, he is capable of Hajj?' He said: 'Woe to you! It is not as you think. You see a man who has abundant wealth, more than the provisions and the mount, yet he does not perform Hajj until Allah, the Exalted, permits him in that matter.'

key_terms.الْقَدَر: Al-Qadar (Divine Decree/Capacity), referring to a group or concept related to ability

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'capacity' (istita'ah) for Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the juristic definition of *istita'ah* by distinguishing between physical capability and the requisite material means (provisions and transport), while also introducing the theological dimension of divine permission (*mashi'ah*). This hadith is pivotal in Shia fiqh for establishing that Hajj is not obligatory until both external conditions are met and God facilitates the opportunity, a nuance often debated in discussions on the timing of the Hajj obligation. The dialogue with the Qadari highlights the interplay between human effort and divine will in fulfilling religious duties.
